_doc: The numbers mcgyvr sizes and judges a machine with that it cannot read off the machine or the model. The `numbers` block holds some of them, and every entry of it is an estimate: a starting value shipped with mcgyvr, not a reading of your machine. Each is keyed by something every machine has (an engine, a unit's tolerance class), never by a machine's name. To use your own value, write it in numbers.yaml in the config folder ($MCGYVR_HOME, default ~/.mcgyvr), under the number's name and then its key, for example `prefill_class_pct:` and below it `vllm: 12`; your value replaces the estimate. A number of this block that neither file states is refused by name: none of them falls back to a default in code.

warm_decode_class_pct.estimates: How far, in percent, the warm decode speed of a healthy unit of this tolerance class may fall from one start of the unit to the next.
warm_decode_class_pct.used_for: A live probe that finds a unit's warm decode further than this below its locked warm decode pulls the combination the unit runs in, until that combination's validation is committed again. Writing a fleet's lock is refused when a unit's warm decode falls further than this below the baseline its evidence states for it.
warm_decode_class_pct.note: A starting value, not a reading of your machine. The spread between starts may differ with the engine version, the model and what else the machine is doing.

prefill_class_pct.estimates: How far, in percent, the prefill speed of a healthy unit of this tolerance class may fall from one start of the unit to the next.
prefill_class_pct.used_for: A live probe that finds a unit's prefill further than this below its locked prefill pulls the combination the unit runs in, until that combination's validation is committed again.
prefill_class_pct.note: A starting value, not a reading of your machine. The spread between starts may differ with the engine version, the model and what else the machine is doing.

runtime_resident_gb.estimates: Host memory, in GiB, that a llama.cpp server holds beyond the expert weights it keeps in host memory.
runtime_resident_gb.used_for: Added to the host memory a llama.cpp unit is sized to need when some of its experts stay in host memory; charged only then, and never to a unit of another engine.
runtime_resident_gb.note: A starting value, not a reading of your machine. It may differ with the model and the context size.

link_gib_s.estimates: How much data, in GiB per second, a link of this class carries between two cards: the usable rate of the bus between two cards in one machine, or of the network between two machines.
link_gib_s.used_for: Priced into the traffic between the shards of a model split across cards: the time a split spends moving data between its shards is the size of that data over this rate, plus the latency of each crossing. The first reading of your own link replaces it.
link_gib_s.note: A starting value, not a reading of your machine. It is taken from the published rate of a class of link (a PCIe 3.0 x16 bus, and one gigabit Ethernet), and your link may be faster or slower. The first reading of your own link replaces it, and you can set your own value in numbers.yaml before then.

link_latency_us.estimates: How long, in microseconds, a small message takes to cross a link of this class between two cards: the fixed cost of a transfer, however small.
link_latency_us.used_for: Added to each crossing between the shards of a model split across cards, so a split that sends many small messages is priced by the number of its crossings and not only by their size. The first reading of your own link replaces it.
link_latency_us.note: A starting value, not a reading of your machine. The latency of a link depends on its hardware, its driver and what else uses it. The first reading of your own link replaces it, and you can set your own value in numbers.yaml before then.

shard_allowance_gib.estimates: Card memory, in GiB, that each card of a tensor split holds beyond its share of the weights and its cache: its CUDA context, compute scratch, and the buffers its all-reduces go through. For vLLM, each rank of any split; for llama.cpp, each card of its --split-mode tensor.
shard_allowance_gib.used_for: Added to the weights and cache of each shard of a vLLM unit split across cards, and of each card of a llama.cpp unit under --split-mode tensor, when the shard's card room is sized. A llama.cpp layer split charges the single-card allowance instead.
shard_allowance_gib.note: A starting value, not a reading of your machine. It may differ with the model, the context size, the batch, the engine version and the width of the split. llama.cpp's is its single-card scratch and context bound (768 MiB) with room for the meta device's reduction buffers. Set your own value in numbers.yaml when your own reading of a card's memory differs.
